title: Head of MOFCOM Department of American and Oceanian Affairs Elaborates on Outcomes of Eighth Round of China-U.S. Economic and Trade Consultations
date_evidence: (Released on September 28); consultations held From September 20 to 23; meta-PubDate: 2026-10-12 14:37
key_claim: China's commerce ministry says that at the eighth round the two sides agreed to extend the Kuala Lumpur arrangement, which had suspended certain tariff and non-tariff measures until 10 November 2026, to 10 January 2027 and to keep discussing a mutually agreed solution; the page does not mention export controls, rare earths or licences.
frame_summary: The ministry presents the extension as a bridge that gives enterprises a stable and predictable policy environment while talks on a further extension continue.
verbatim_quote: In this round of economic and trade consultations, China and the U.S. agreed to extend the Kuala Lumpur economic and trade arrangement to January 10, 2027 and continue to actively discuss this matter with the aim of reaching a mutually agreed solution.
verbatim_list: In October 2025, China and the U.S. reached a joint arrangement in Kuala Lumpur to address their respective economic and trade concerns, suspending the implementation of certain tariff and non-tariff measures on the two sides until November 10, 2026.
It is believed that the two sides will continue to work towards a positive solution for further extension through high-level economic and trade interactions before the end of the year.
a relatively stable and predictable policy environment for cooperation between enterprises of the two sides
notes: Fetched 04/11/2026, full page. Date conflict recorded: the page text ends (Released on September 28) while a meta PubDate reads 2026-10-12; the release date in the text is used.

title: U.S.-China trade truce extension: Why compliance teams can't wait until January for still-expiring Section 301 exclusions
key_claim: The compliance publisher lists three US measures that expire on 9 and 10 November, two months before the broader truce ends on 10 January 2027, including 178 remaining Section 301 exclusions and the BIS Affiliates Rule suspension, and notes the extension had not been formally documented by executive order or Federal Register notice.
frame_summary: The publisher argues that the extended truce does not extend the underlying legal instruments, so compliance teams should plan to the November dates.
verbatim_quote: The 178 remaining Section 301 China exclusions expire on November 10, 2026.
verbatim_list: Three U.S. measures expire November 9 and 10, two months before the broader trade truce ends in January.
As of this writing, that extension hasn’t been formally documented through an executive order or Federal Register notice.
notes: Fetched 04/11/2026, full page. The page also says China's rare earth export controls begin on 10 November; that line is not used.

title: The November deadline hanging over this week's Trump-Xi meeting
key_claim: A bank geo-economics analyst, writing before the September summit, says China's temporary suspension of additional rare earth export controls expires on 10 November and expects the issue to be handled through another temporary extension.
frame_summary: The bank frames the rare earth deadline as a summit item to be resolved by a further temporary extension.
verbatim_quote: China’s temporary suspension of additional export controls on rare earth minerals expires on 10 November, giving the two leaders seven weeks to deal with it when they meet in Washington on Thursday.
verbatim_list: His central view is that the rare-earth issue will most likely be dealt with through another temporary extension of China's export controls.
notes: Fetched 04/11/2026, full page. Pre-summit forecast; its outcome statements are predictions. No byline author shown.

title: China's Rare Earth Magnet Exports Hit 2026 High, Up 23% MoM and 6.7% YoY Amid Trade Progress
key_claim: The metals data provider reports, from customs data, that China's rare earth permanent magnet exports in September 2026 reached 6,165.12 mt, up 23% on the month and 6.7% on the year, a 2026 high.
frame_summary: The provider reads the September data as a sign of trade progress and a stable fourth-quarter stockpiling phase.
verbatim_quote: [SMM Rare Earth Flash] According to customs data, China's rare earth permanent magnet exports in September 2026 reached 6,165.12 mt, up 23% MoM and up 6.7% YoY, hitting a new high for rare earth permanent magnet exports in 2026.
verbatim_list: Through September, rare earth permanent magnet exports in 2026 totaled 48,055 mt, up 20% from the same period last year.
notes: Fetched 04/11/2026, full page (three sentences). Totals are for all destinations.

title: China Export Control Suspension: November 2026 Scenarios
key_claim: A Seoul compliance advisory that read the primary texts says MOFCOM Announcement No. 70 still reads until 10 November 2026 and No. 72 until 27 November 2026, that MOFCOM's policy release list shows no instrument moving either date, and that general licences are reported as few, tied to named customers and valid one year, with no public list of holders.
frame_summary: The advisory argues that the political extension to 10 January 2027 is not a legal one, so the November dates stand until an instrument says otherwise.
verbatim_quote: MOFCOM and Customs Announcement No. 70 of 2025, which suspends China's October 2025 export-control additions, still reads “until November 10, 2026”.
verbatim_list: MOFCOM Announcement No. 72 of 2025, which suspends the US-specific prohibition on gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials, still reads “until November 27, 2026”.
They are reported as few, tied to named customers and valid one year, granted to a handful of large rare earth magnet producers, by the press accounts we found.
There is no public list of holders, and no source says whether one would cover No. 57 or No. 61 items if those resume.
Some press reports say the rare earth suspension was extended; the primary texts we read do not.
notes: Fetched 04/11/2026, full page. Small advisory publisher; its reading of the MOFCOM texts is cross-checked against E+E Leader and Thomson Reuters, and the MOFCOM page itself does not mention export controls.

title: Rare Earth Truce Is Extended, but Its Legal Deadlines Stand
key_claim: The trade publication reports that as of 29 October neither government had published the legal changes carrying their export-control suspensions past 9 and 10 November, that the Chinese Commerce Ministry statement refers to tariff and non-tariff measures in general without naming export controls or rare earths, and that Beijing's suspended controls would apply again from 11 November without a new instrument.
frame_summary: The publication argues that the extension is a political announcement whose legal deadlines still stand until instruments are published.
verbatim_quote: As of Oct. 29, however, neither government had published the legal changes that would carry its own export-control suspensions past Nov. 9 and Nov. 10.
verbatim_list: The statement refers to tariff and non-tariff measures in general.
It does not name export controls or rare earths.

Beijing’s suspended controls would apply again from Nov. 11 without a new instrument, bringing licensing back for holmium, erbium, thulium, europium and ytterbium, and for battery inputs where China dominates, including the graphite anode material that U.S. producers are trying to replace.
Last year's suspension was published on the day it took effect, so a late notice is possible.
notes: Fetched 04/11/2026, full page. Desk byline (Supply Chain + Procurement). No machine-readable date on the page; the visible dateline is used.

title: China Rare-Earth Magnet Exports to US Drop Before Xi-Trump Meet
date_evidence: Bloomberg News Sun, September 20, 2026 at 8:28 PM EDT
key_claim: Bloomberg reports that magnet shipments to the US fell 21% in August to 512 tons, average about 504 tons a month this year against 621 tons in 2024, and that China hopes to offer more licences for rare earth exports as a bargaining chip.
frame_summary: Bloomberg presents licence volumes as a bargaining chip that Beijing can turn up or down around the summit.
verbatim_quote: Shipments of magnets to the US dropped 21% in August to 512 tons from the month before, according to Chinese customs data released on Sunday.
verbatim_list: China hopes to offer more licenses for rare earth exports as a bargaining chip in talks, people with familiar with the matter said, without disclosing what Beijing would demand in return.
They're running at an average of about 504 tons a month this year, although that's still below 621 tons in 2024 before the curbs.
notes: Fetched 04/11/2026; Yahoo syndication of Bloomberg News, possibly a partial excerpt (ends with a Story Continues marker). Dateline only; no machine-readable date shown.

title: Congress Moves to Break China Rare Earth Grip Before November Deadline
date_evidence: meta article:published_time: 2026-10-06T15:48:50-04:00; Published: Oct 06 2026, 3:48 PM EDT
key_claim: The technology outlet reports that the April 2025 Chinese controls on seven elements were never suspended, that no formal extension of the suspension had been announced at the time, and that after 10 November China could extend the suspension, selectively reactivate specific controls or fully restore the October 2025 measures.
frame_summary: The outlet frames the November date as a hard stop for the suspended October 2025 measures while the April 2025 licensing regime stays in force regardless.
verbatim_quote: After November 10, China could extend the suspension, selectively reactivate specific controls, or fully restore the October 2025 measures.
verbatim_list: But that reprieve has a hard stop — and the April 2025 controls on seven elements were never suspended at all.
